Title: Diagnosis of test `testGetLineNumberWithCR`
Details: The test `testGetLineNumberWithCR` is designed to check the line number reported by the `CSVParser` when parsing input strings with carriage return (`\r`) as the line separator. The test creates a parser with the input string "a\rb\rc" and a `CSVFormat` that has `\r` as the line separator.

Looking at the code, `CSVParser.getLineNumber()` delegates to `lexer.getLineNumber()`, which further delegates to `in.getLineNumber()`, where `in` is an `ExtendedBufferedReader`. The `ExtendedBufferedReader.getLineNumber()` simply returns the `lineCounter`.

However, examining the `ExtendedBufferedReader.read()` method, the `lineCounter` only increments when the current character read is a newline `\n`. It does not increment for carriage return `\r`.

This behavior causes the line counting to fail when the line separator is `\r`, which is the case in this test. The input string uses `\r` as line separators, but the `lineCounter` only increments on `\n`, resulting in the `getLineNumber()` not incrementing as expected. Therefore, the test expecting line number to increase with `\r` line separators fails.

The root cause is that `ExtendedBufferedReader` only counts newline (`\n`) characters as new lines and ignores carriage return (`\r`) line endings, causing the line number reporting to be incorrect for CR line separators.

The correction should involve modifying `ExtendedBufferedReader.read()` to also count `\r` as new lines if the CSVFormat or parser is configured to handle those line separators.

Suggested methods to fix:
org.apache.commons.csv.ExtendedBufferedReader.read()

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
